IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA  CIVIL APPELLATE JURISDICTION  CIVIL APPEAL NO. 7338 OF 2024  (Arising out of SLP (C)NO. 8537/2023)
 ISHWAR SINGH APPELL  VERSUS  THE LAND ACQUISITION COLLECTOR, HP PWD & ORS. RESPON  O R D E R Leave granted.
This matter relates to the land acquisition in the State of Himachal Pradesh.

Notification under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 was issued by the State on 16.04.2004 for acquiring the land bearing in Khasra No.1606 measuring 918 Sq. M. in U.P. Mohal Saraswati Nagar, Tehsil Jubbal District, Shimla.
Subsequently, the Collector (Respondent No.1) had passed an award granting total compensation of Rs.7,990/- to the land acquired of the appellant.
Being aggrieved, the petitioner challenged the matter under section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act to the Reference Court.
The Reference Court vide order dated 13.07.2012 enhanced the amount to Rs.3398.25 per centiare apart from the solatium.
Against the order of the Reference Court, the State filed the Statutory appeal before the High Court.
The High Court vide its order dated 08.06.2020 has decreased the amount from Rs.3398.35 to Rs.1699/- per centiar.
We have gone through the order dated 13.07.2012 of the Reference Court as well as the order dated 08.06.2020 of the High Court.

Whereas the Reference Court while fixing the amount at Rs.3398.25 per centiare has gone on certain parameters i.e. one year market value, the High Court, on the other hand, has not given any reason whatsoever while decreasing the value/compensation of the land from Rs. 3398.35 to Rs. 1699/- per centiar.
The amount fixed by the Reference Court at Rs.3398.25 per centiare is a possible view.

It is not an arbitrary determination of the value of the Ishwar Singh vs The Land Acquisition Collector on 11 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18625956/
